name: expiry_eve_entry_v1
question: Is the history's entry price executable? L1's history (expiry_eve_law_v2) sells each leg at the eve's bhavcopy close minus (0.05 + max(0.05, 0.2% of the close)); the forward sleeves sell at the real 15:20 bid minus 0.05. This measures the difference on the same strikes on the same eve
why: the L1 evidence audit (docs/reports/2026-10-04_l1_evidence_audit.md, section 10): a bhavcopy close is a last trade on only 27% of NSE option rows, so the entry price is the largest unverified approximation in L1's history. A paired difference on the same strikes resolves in weeks; a P&L-only forward test would need about 300

population.eves: every session before an expiry of these instruments on which a registered expiry-seller sleeve (docs/prereg/expiry_seller_v*.json) opened; one observation per instrument and expiry, from the earliest open event for it
population.legs: the two short legs at target delta 0.20 (one CE, one PE) that the sleeve picked from the Kotak snapshot nearest 15:20 by the history's strike rule

measures.executable_credit_bps: the sum over the two short legs of the recorded fill (bid - 0.05), in bps of the snapshot's index spot
measures.history_credit_bps: the sum over the same two strikes of the eve's bhavcopy close minus leg_cost(close) = 0.05 + max(0.05, 0.002 x close), in bps of the eve's official index close (nse_index_close; for SENSEX the bhavcopy underlying)
measures.d_bps: history_credit_bps - executable_credit_bps: positive when the history assumed a better sale than the market offered
measures.exclusion: an eve where either strike has no bhavcopy row with contracts > 0 and close > 0 is excluded from the test and counted: the history would not have priced that leg
measures.secondary: the two legs' payout at the expiry's official close and at the sleeves' registered 15:00-15:29 mean, in bps of the entry spot; reported, not tested

test.series: weekly: per ISO week of the expiry, the mean d_bps across that week's eves
test.nw: Newey-West t, Bartlett kernel, lags floor(4 x (weeks/100)^(2/9)), as research/edges.hac_mean
test.equivalent: t of (d_bps + 2) > 1.645 and t of (d_bps - 2) < -1.645 (two one-sided tests)

sample_size.reestimate_rule: after the first 10 eves: n = min(120, max(40, ceil(1.6 x ((1.645 + 0.842) x sd10 / 2)^2))), sd10 the sample sd of d_bps over those 10 eves; it can only raise n
sample_size.extend_rule: if the result at n eves and 12 weeks is inconclusive, continue once to max(80, n), capped at 120, and decide there; inconclusive then is the result
sample_size.interim: before the decision point the report shows only the eves collected, the excluded count and the current n: no mean, sd or t

decision.overstated: L1's historical edge is overstated by an entry-price artifact: recompute L1's pooled result with the mean d_bps subtracted from every trade and register expiry_eve_law_v3; L1 keeps a caveat until then
decision.equivalent: the history's entry convention is validated: clear L1's non-executable-entry caveat
decision.understated: the history's entry convention was conservative: clear the caveat and record by how much
decision.inconclusive: L1 keeps its caveat; any follow-up is a new spec

out_of_scope: live trading; any change to the sleeves' registered rules; promotion of any strategy
changes: evaluated once at the decision point; a different rule is a new spec
